title: Sync playbook for PRD scope adjustments and cross-team sign-off ladder
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: When PRDs evolve during implementation (scope carve-outs, API surface compromises, or structured-output gating), we lack a lightweight, deterministic process that (a) communicates required trade-offs to engineering and design, (b) captures legal/data residency constraints early, and (c) produces a single acceptance artifact that downstream teams can rely on for rollout and audits.

Goal: Define and trial a 'Sync Playbook' that formalizes cross-team checkpoints and creates a one-page sign-off ladder for PRD scope changes. The playbook should cover: scope-change classification (minor, material, blocking), required reviewers per class, minimum acceptance criteria per discipline (Eng/Design/Legal/SRE/QA), fallback policies, and an escalation path for unresolved disagreements.

Scope: This ticket covers authoring the playbook, aligning leads from Eng/Design/Legal to the ladder and acceptance checklist, and piloting the process on the structured-output PRD (see links). It does NOT include tooling automation (that will be a follow-up).

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Time-to-decision target: 5 business days for 'material' changes; 24-48 hours for 'minor' clarifications.
- Engineering budget: maintain 95th percentile latency budget and cost-per-token threshold; any proposed changes that increase infra cost >10% require separate cost-approved PRD.
- Legal/regulatory: private/VPC or data residency additions trigger automatic 'material' classification.
- Design accessibility: visual changes must pass a11y contrast and keyboard-flow checks before sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page 'Sign-off Ladder' document (PDF/Confluence) exists and is agreed by Eng, Design, Legal, and SRE leads.
Scope-change taxonomy defined for: minor, material, blocking (with examples).
Reviewer matrix mapping review timebox and primary contacts for each taxonomy level.
Minimum discipline-specific acceptance checklist captured for Eng, Design, Legal, QA, and SRE.
Pilot run completed on structured-output PRD: at least one material and one minor change processed through the playbook with documented outcomes.
Rollout criteria for the playbook: playbook approved by Product Council and included as PRD template appendix.
